narrative.overview: A tactile, paper-driven interface that feels like flipping through a vintage department store catalog — warm cream surfaces, bold uppercase labels, and hard-offset shadows that give each card a physical presence on the page. The design treats the 120-product catalog as a literal shelf: square tiles, department groups, and a persistent sidebar grid keep the inventory visible at all times.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper palette with terracotta accent and forest green secondary
Square catalog tiles with level-based color grading (lv0–lv3)
Side-by-side comparison columns with semantic source borders
Persistent left catalog sidebar, mobile: stacked

rules.name: The Source-Color Rule
rules.body: Border-left color on tiles is semantic, not decorative: green = found in both searches, blue = keyword-only, terracotta = LAYA-only. Removing these borders destroys the comparison mechanic.

rules.name: The Level-Heat Rule
rules.body: Tile background shifts from cool gray (lv0) through warm cream (lv1) to amber (lv2) and terracotta-accented (lv3) — higher score = warmer surface. Never invert: lv0 must be the coolest, lv3 the warmest.

rules.name: The Hard Shadow Rule
rules.body: The 4px offset shadow is the system's depth language. Soft blur shadows would read as generic/material and break the catalog identity. Zero-offset colored halos are decoration — banned.

rules.name: The Catalog Label Rule
rules.body: Every uppercase tracked label is a catalog artifact — selo, exemplos-label, categoria-title, contador-titulo. Keep them short (1–2 words) and always uppercase with letter-spacing.

dos: Do preserve the 2-column comparison layout — it is the product's core mechanic
Do keep the sidebar catalog visible at all times; it contextualizes every search
Do use the source-border colors (OK/green, keyword/blue, terracotta) consistently on tiles in both columns
Do maintain the hard 4px shadow vocabulary across all cards
Do use Bricolage Grotesque for all uppercase labels and the hero title
donts: Don't introduce rounded corners on cards or buttons — zero radius is the identity
Don't replace the hard offset shadow with soft blur or layered shadows
Don't add gradient text, glass effects, or backdrop-filter decoration
Don't use emoji as icon substitutes — the system uses text labels and semantic colors
Don't hide the catalog sidebar on desktop — it's always open (catalog-open class)
